questions.q: What are the three goals that make up the CIA triad?
options: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
Confidentiality, Inspection, Authentication
Compliance, Integrity, Authorization
Control, Inventory, Audit
questions.explain: The CIA triad is Confidentiality (who can see data), Integrity (data hasn't been tampered with), and Availability (authorized users can access it when needed).

questions.q: The 2017 Equifax breach exposed roughly 147 million people's personal data without altering it or taking any system offline. Which leg of the CIA triad did this primarily violate?
options: Availability, because the website was slow afterward
Integrity, because records were changed
Confidentiality, because unauthorized parties could read data they shouldn't have had access to
None of the three — a data breach isn't a CIA triad issue
questions.explain: Nothing was altered or taken down; the core failure was that unauthorized parties could view sensitive data, which is a confidentiality violation.

questions.q: An attacker quietly changes a vendor's bank routing number inside a company's accounting system, without stealing any files or disrupting access. Which leg of the triad is this?
options: Confidentiality
Availability
Integrity
This isn't a security issue since nothing was taken
questions.explain: Unauthorized modification of data, even without theft or downtime, is an integrity violation — the data is no longer trustworthy.

questions.q: A DDoS attack floods a company's website with junk traffic so real customers can't load the page. Which leg of the CIA triad does this attack type target?
options: Integrity, because the page content changes
Availability, because authorized users can no longer access the system
Confidentiality, because traffic is being read
Accountability, which isn't part of the triad
questions.explain: A DDoS attack doesn't read or alter data — it denies legitimate access, which is exactly what availability protects against.

questions.q: Which pairing correctly matches a security control to the CIA triad leg it primarily protects?
options: Encryption protects confidentiality; hashing/digital signatures protect integrity; backups and redundancy protect availability
Encryption protects availability; backups protect confidentiality; hashing protects nothing
Hashing protects availability; encryption protects integrity
All controls only ever protect confidentiality
questions.explain: Encryption keeps data unreadable to unauthorized parties (confidentiality), hashing/signatures detect tampering (integrity), and backups/redundancy keep systems reachable (availability).
